correctness.rationale: The 16-vertex graph, ten-vertex complement neighborhoods and 11,804 simplices are rebuilt from XOR adjacency. An exhaustive acyclic matching gives exactly critical multiplicities 1,6,137 in dimensions 0,3,4, after checking every one of 65,680 Hasse covers. Signed integral gradient-path cancellation produces a 6x137 attaching-degree matrix with explicitly reproduced determinant-one 6x6 minor (columns 2,4,9,10,23,26). Since the three-skeleton is a wedge of six 3-spheres and π3 of that wedge is Z^6, unimodular cell-basis changes split off six contractible attachments and leave 131 degree-four spheres. Published integral combinatorial Alexander duality for 16 vertices yields reduced Z^131 in dominance degree nine with no other homology. Direct full-chain mod-two Betti ranks and a separate enumeration of 65,536 dominating-complement candidates corroborate Euler and dimensions. No finite testing is extrapolated to arbitrary graphs.

originality.rationale: A checked published same-graph RESULT.md establishes the Lovasz neighborhood complex of the five-regular Clebsch graph, not of its ten-regular complement; it expressly excludes that complement. Primary Matsushita–Wakatsuki gives duality but not this graph calculation; Shukla degree hypotheses fail. published-finding corpus searches under full graph name, halved 5-cube, dominance, Hom(K2), Dowker and exact numerical ranks yielded no covering assertion. Conclusions remain conditional on the inspected corpus and do not constitute a global novelty guarantee.
residual_risks: Poorly indexed independent numerical calculation of the halved five-cube neighborhood complex could exist.
Search result rankings and accessible material are not mathematically exhaustive; literature uniqueness is not asserted.

value.rationale: The ten-regular complement of the five-regular Clebsch graph is a canonical 16-vertex strongly regular graph, also the halved five-cube. Its integral open-neighborhood homotopy type is a natural exact invariant, and the 131-sphere result is substantially more than enumerating simplices. The calculation also determines the complete integral dominance homology of the dual five-regular graph, a concrete new graph instance beyond the general published Alexander-duality theorem. No infinite-family significance or equivariant type is claimed.
